name: New Nordic cuisine
region: Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo and the Nordic coast
summary: A tasting-menu kitchen that cooks only what grows, swims or is foraged in the Nordic region, in the season of the day. Twelve chefs signed the Manifesto for the New Nordic Kitchen in 2004. Vinegar, ferments and wild plants replace lemon and olive oil.

philosophy.core_thesis: A kitchen of one place and one season: the cold, the short summer and the long winter of the North set the menu, and the cook preserves the summer for the winter.
design_principles: Use only produce of the Nordic region; replace lemon with vinegar, sorrel or fermented juice, and olive oil with butter or cold-pressed rapeseed oil.
Forage wild plants, berries, mushrooms and shellfish, and change the menu with the season.
Preserve the summer: pickle, salt, smoke, dry and ferment, so that a winter menu tastes of the summer.
Cook on wood and embers, and keep the taste of smoke and char.
Show the ingredient as it grew: a whole radish, a leaf, a shell, on a plate of stone, wood or hand-made ceramic.
Serve many small courses, some eaten by hand, in a room of wood and daylight.
Keep a research kitchen for fermentation; a new garum, koji or vinegar is part of the menu.
anti_patterns: Lemon, olive oil and other imported staples
Foie gras, caviar or other luxury goods for their price
A cream or butter sauce that covers the ingredient
The same menu all the year
Laboratory gels and foams as the point of the dish
A white porcelain plate with a gold rim

plating.composition: A small, natural-looking composition: a few elements in a line or a loose cluster, often covered by leaves or flowers, on a wide hand-made plate.
plating.plate: A hand-thrown stoneware plate or bowl in grey, brown or black, a flat stone, a wooden board or a bed of moss or hay.
plating.portion: Twenty to forty courses of 10 to 60 g each; a main piece rarely more than 80 g.
plating.height: Low: the food lies 5 to 20 mm high, with leaves and flowers as the top layer.
rules: Put the vegetable or the shellfish in its natural form: whole, with its leaves or in its shell.
Cover the main element with leaves, petals or a sheet of something dried, so that the guest finds it.
Use a vessel made by a local potter, or a stone, wood or hay that comes from the landscape.
Leave half the plate empty and keep the sauce in a small pool or under the food.
Serve some courses on a bed of moss, stones or ice, for the hands, with no cutlery.

pantry.rule: Take every item from the Nordic region and its season; give acid from vinegar, sorrel, unripe fruit or ferment, not from citrus.

technique.bases: Vinegars and fermented juices of berries and fruit, garums of fish and meat, koji made on barley and peas, and smoked and dried fish.
technique.details: A dusting of dried berry or cep powder, a glaze of fermented juice, burnt hay, an edible flower, a brown butter.

flavour.profile: Clean, sour and herbal, with the umami of ferments and the smoke of embers.
flavour.balance: Acid leads; umami from garum and koji; little sweet and almost no heat.
flavour.fat: Butter, cream and rapeseed oil in small quantities; 20 to 35 per cent of the energy of a course.
flavour.seasoning: Salt, vinegar, garum, dried herbs and berries, juniper, wood sorrel and the oil of conifer needles.

palette.strategy: Use the colours of the Nordic landscape: dark stoneware, grey stone, the green of leaves and moss, and one bright berry or flower.

service.format: A fixed tasting menu by season: the cooks bring and explain many of the courses at the table.
service.courses: Twenty to forty small courses in three or four acts, with bread, a few main courses and two or three desserts.
service.tableware: Hand-thrown stoneware by local potters, stones, wooden boards, linen napkins, no tablecloth.
service.setting: A former warehouse with wood, daylight and plain Danish furniture; cooks in aprons serve with the waiters.

canonical_works.work: Manifesto for the New Nordic Kitchen
canonical_works.maker: Claus Meyer and twelve Nordic chefs

canonical_works.work: Noma: Time and Place in Nordic Cuisine

evidence.title: Inside Noma: a course at the table

emotion.target_response: The feeling of a walk on the coast in one season: cold air, wet leaves, smoke and something sour.

use_cases: a tasting menu of a Nordic restaurant
a food photograph on dark stoneware
a menu that uses only local and seasonal produce
avoid_when: the brief wants citrus, olive oil or a Mediterranean pantry
the brief wants a rich classic sauce
the brief is street or fast food

modifiers.request: more plants, no meat or fish
modifiers.how: Remove the venison, the shellfish and the fish garums; make every course from vegetables, grains and ferments.
Keep the foraged plants and the seasonal menu, and allow olive oil, lemon and the herbs of the South.

sources.title: René Redzepi, Noma: Time and Place in Nordic Cuisine (Phaidon, 2010)
